review_notes:
I read the whole file (lines 1–101) and searched the working tree for uses of each declaration. I also read the definitions of constituentLines, constituent, fixArray and conditionalProbability.

The file has no @[simp] attributes. I found no concrete simp-interface defect in it.

- not_mem_constituentLines_iff, not_mem_iff_of_direction_agreement and not_mem_fixArray_iff are used by explicit `rw`, `simp only [...]` or direct application. Nothing outside this file calls them through `simp`.
- not_mem_fixArray_iff has a side hypothesis `hL : L.1 ∈ D`. The only `simp only` call that uses it is in gated_count_fixArray, and it supplies the lemma fully instantiated. Tagging it @[simp] would depend on the discharger proving `L.1 ∈ D` and would not obviously help any current use, so I did not recommend it.
- conditionalProbability_gate and gated_count_fixArray are one-off rewrites with hypotheses. Their `if` right-hand sides are the intended normal form. I saw no competing rules, expansion problem or rewrite cycle.
- Several call sites elsewhere (CandidateGlobalLineModel, CandidateGlobalLineMean) apply these lemmas directly rather than through `simp`.

Remaining uncertainty: I did not check whether other files carry simp lemmas about constituentLines membership that would interact with these. The grep showed none in the Construction directory.
